digest:
Two days in AI right now feel like two months anywhere else. The agent stack keeps compressing — what needed a research team last year ships as an API flag this week — and the money is following the same gradient, from models to the scaffolding around them.

**Agents**

The big story is [Agentic coding goes mainstream](https://example.com/agents) — the tools stopped being demos and started being infrastructure. Meanwhile [a new eval suite drops](https://example.com/evals) and, honestly, it's about time: most agent benchmarks still measure vibes. The skeptical read: everyone claims autonomy, few publish failure rates.

**Startups**

On the money side, [Seed rounds cluster around agent infra](https://example.com/funding) — investors are betting the picks-and-shovels layer consolidates first. [One stealth launch worth watching](https://example.com/launch) suggests the next wave is agents that write their own tools instead of calling yours.

So what? The pattern is the same everywhere: the abstraction is moving up. Build for the layer above the model, not the model itself.
